It's unlikely that you have a tick infestation inside your house - more likely the ones you're finding crawled off of your dog or your shoes/pants when you came in from outside. No tick medication is going to prevent that from happening. You'll either have to prevent your dog from roaming free during tick season (basically until the first freeze), or give her a quick combing with a fine-toothed comb after she's done running around collecting ticks.

If you venture outdoors much yourself, be aware that ticks dwell at the edges of practically any plant you're walking by, and will hitch a ride once you brush past. They are perfectly happy drinking your blood instead of your dog's. In my experience most will hop on your shoes, then crawl up your pants or legs, then stop at the first border they hit (typically the elastic in your underwear), attach themselves, and start sucking.

People who haven't grown up around ubiquitous summer ticks freak out over a bite, but to anyone who's lived in the South they are typically about as worrisome as a mosquito bite. I've yanked off dozens (hundreds counting the tiny mite-sized ones) of attached ticks with my fingers, never took any special care, never had any problem. My ex, on the other hand, got Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever and was hospitalized, so YMMV.

What I learned is that prevention is the best cure. Wear long pants, any time you venture outside strip down and check your entire body afterward - you WILL find ticks if you spend much time out. Do the same for your dog. You will likely miss some; check her again in the evening for attached ones, then yank and flush them. Ears (as you have discovered) and in between toes or in the bottoms of their feet are prime spots.

If you are ever unlucky enough to unwittingly stumble through a nest of baby ticks and find there are about 200 of them attached to your leg (as I once did), shave them off. You might consider shaving off your dog's hair for the summer as that will help some (though watch out for sunburn).

Finally, tick bites itch like hell for a good month afterward. Fuck ticks.
